title: An if or match whose branches construct a value class, one from a literal, crashes erasure when the result is used as a receiver (mergePrefixAndArgs: unsupported tps)
oracle: reference compile of a valid program
generator: wave4/harness/programs/Gen.scala, value classes in switch arms of a guard (round 5 program, constructs of rounds 2 and the value class grammar meeting)
signature: ref|crash|CRASH scala.reflect.internal.FatalError: mergePrefixAndArgs(List(ErasedValueType(class N, Int), ErasedValueType(class N, Int(7))), covariant, Depth(1)): unsupported tps @ Typers$Typer.typedMatch
detail: With case class V0(u: Int) extends AnyVal, (if (a > 0) V0(b) else V0(7)) == V0(5) and (if (a > 0) V0(b) else V0(7)).u do not compile: FatalError 'mergePrefixAndArgs(List(ErasedValueType(class V0, Int), ErasedValueType(class V0, Int(7))), covariant, Depth(1)): unsupported tps' during erasure. When erasure retypes a value class injection it gives it ErasedValueType(V0, result.tpe) with the argument's type unwidened (Erasure.scala, the InjectDerivedValue case of the erasure typer), so V0(7) gets ErasedValueType(V0, Int(7)). Where the conditional is a receiver its type is recomputed as a lub of the branches, and lub cannot merge two ErasedValueTypes that differ only in that constant. Both branches literal (V0(3) / V0(7)) crashes as well; a match instead of an if too; assigning the conditional to a val of type V0 first does not. Ordinary code with a default value class value in one branch reaches it.
fix_sketch: Widen the argument type when retyping the injection: ErasedValueType(tref.sym, result.tpe.widen) (or use argPt). No compatibility cost.
